newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up, trade quiet on Thai watch.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up, trade quiet on Thai watch.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were quoted higher at the close after tracking a rise in Tokyo futures, dealers said.
They said trade was thin with players sidelined to watch possibilities of further government support for prices in the Thai market, which could make Malaysian rubber competitive.
"There was covering for the (SMR) 10 and 20 by local agents," said a dealer, adding that this could not be quantified.
Traders said the volatility in US/Asian currencies was also worrying. "It's very difficult for planning," said one.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS1 buyer at 275.50 cents ($1.11) a kg, up 2.50 cents from Thursday. June SMR 20 buyer rose 2.0 cents to 262.50 cents.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 262, SMR CV at 273, SMR L at 309, SMR 5 at 273, SMR 10 at 263 and drum latex at 230.
The INRO five-day average rose to 209.45 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 15, compared to 208.17 on May 14. The daily indicator climbed to 214.18 from 210.51 previously.
